WITH fee_rates AS (
  SELECT
    orderslink,
    rebtotal,
    CASE
      WHEN feerate IS NOT NULL AND rebrate IS NOT NULL THEN feerate - rebrate
    END AS net_fee_rate
  FROM fees
),
per_order AS (
  SELECT
    orderslink,
    AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebate,
    AVG(net_fee_rate) AS avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM fee_rates
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(net_fee_rate) AS overall_avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM fee_rates
),
above AS (
  SELECT p.avg_rebate, p.avg_net_fee_rate, o.overall_avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM per_order AS p
  CROSS JOIN overall AS o
  WHERE p.avg_net_fee_rate > o.overall_avg_net_fee_rate
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_rebate) AS mean_of_order_average_rebates,
  AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) AS mean_of_order_average_net_fee_rates,
  AVG(avg_net_fee_rate - overall_avg_net_fee_rate) AS mean_excess_net_fee_rate
FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: A net fee rate is defined only when both feerate and rebrate are present; SQL AVG skips missing values, and orderslink NULL values form one group as requested. The overall average weights each fee record equally, while the final means weight each qualifying order group equally.
